new.vignette: An 8-year-old girl has progressive ataxia, dysarthria, vertical supranuclear gaze palsy, and splenomegaly. Cultured skin fibroblasts show intense perinuclear filipin staining caused by lysosomal accumulation of unesterified cholesterol.
new.lead_in: Which cellular process is most directly impaired in this disorder?

options.A: Intracellular trafficking of unesterified cholesterol and other lipid cargo out of late endosomal-lysosomal compartments by NPC1/NPC2
options.B: Lysosomal hydrolysis of sphingomyelin by acid sphingomyelinase
options.C: Receptor-mediated endocytosis of circulating LDL through the LDL receptor
options.D: Esterification of free cholesterol in the endoplasmic reticulum by acyl-CoA:cholesterol acyltransferase
options.E: Peroxisomal beta-oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids

new.tested_construct: Loss of NPC1/NPC2 function causing lysosomal accumulation of unesterified cholesterol and other lipid cargo
new.educational_objective: Recognize Niemann-Pick disease type C as an NPC1/NPC2 loss-of-function disorder in which defective intracellular lipid trafficking produces lysosomal accumulation of unesterified cholesterol and other lipid cargo.

existing.vignette: An 8-year-old girl has progressive clumsiness, ataxia, dysarthria, and difficulty making rapid vertical eye movements. Examination shows splenomegaly. Her school performance has gradually declined.
existing.lead_in: Which cellular abnormality most likely causes this disorder?

options.A: Deficiency of acid sphingomyelinase causing sphingomyelin accumulation in macrophages
options.B: Failure of NPC1/NPC2-dependent trafficking of cholesterol and other lipids out of lysosomal compartments
options.C: Deficiency of beta-glucocerebrosidase causing glucocerebroside accumulation
options.D: Deficiency of hexosaminidase A causing GM2 ganglioside accumulation
options.E: Deficiency of alpha-galactosidase A causing globotriaosylceramide accumulation

existing.tested_construct: Loss of NPC1 or NPC2 function disrupts intracellular trafficking of lysosomal lipid cargo, causing accumulation of unesterified cholesterol, glycosphingolipids, and gangliosides within lysosomes and progressive visceral and neurologic disease.
existing.educational_objective: Recognize Niemann-Pick type C and connect its characteristic neurologic-visceral phenotype to NPC1/NPC2-dependent lysosomal lipid-trafficking failure.

new.vignette: A 3-year-old boy has recurrent severe bacterial infections without pus formation, persistent leukocytosis, gingival bleeding, and recurrent epistaxis. Flow cytometry shows normal surface expression of beta2 integrins on leukocytes and alpha-IIb-beta3 integrin on platelets, but receptor stimulation fails to induce high-affinity ligand binding in either cell type.
new.lead_in: Which molecular defect best explains both the immune and bleeding manifestations?

options.A: Loss of the beta2-integrin subunit CD18, preventing leukocyte integrin surface expression
options.B: Loss of FERMT3-encoded kindlin-3, impairing inside-out activation of hematopoietic-cell integrins
options.C: Loss of platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa expression with otherwise normal leukocyte integrin activation
options.D: Defective phagocyte NADPH oxidase assembly, preventing the respiratory burst
options.E: Loss of the Golgi GDP-fucose transporter SLC35C1, impairing selectin-ligand fucosylation and leukocyte rolling

new.tested_construct: FERMT3/kindlin-3 deficiency causing defective inside-out integrin activation in leukocytes and platelets
new.educational_objective: Distinguish LAD-III from LAD-I and isolated platelet disorders by recognizing normal integrin surface expression with defective FERMT3/kindlin-3-dependent inside-out activation in both leukocytes and platelets.

existing.vignette: A 10-month-old boy has recurrent bacterial skin and respiratory infections, poor wound healing, persistent leukocytosis, and severe mucosal bleeding despite a normal platelet count. Flow cytometry shows normal surface abundance of CD18-containing β2 integrins on leukocytes and normal αIIbβ3 on platelets. After receptor stimulation, however, both leukocytes and platelets fail to bind their integrin ligands efficiently.
existing.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains the combined immune and bleeding phenotype?

options.A: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency type III due to FERMT3 deficiency
options.B: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency type I due to ITGB2 deficiency
options.C: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency type II due to impaired fucosylation
options.D: Glanzmann thrombasthenia due to quantitative or qualitative αIIbβ3 deficiency

existing.tested_construct: LAD-III results from FERMT3/kindlin-3 deficiency, which prevents inside-out conformational activation of hematopoietic integrins despite preserved surface expression, causing leukocyte dysfunction and a platelet bleeding defect.
existing.educational_objective: Recognize LAD-III when leukocyte and platelet integrins are present but fail activation, producing both infections and bleeding.

new.vignette: A 9-year-old boy has epilepsy beginning in infancy, nonprogressive cerebellar ataxia, sensorineural hearing loss, and chronic salt wasting. Laboratory studies show hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, hypomagnesemia, and low urinary calcium.
new.lead_in: Which renal transport abnormality most directly accounts for the salt-wasting tubulopathy?

options.A: Loss of apical NKCC2-mediated sodium-potassium-chloride uptake in the thick ascending limb
options.B: Loss of apical ROMK-mediated potassium recycling in the thick ascending limb
options.C: Reduced basolateral potassium conductance through Kir4.1 in distal convoluted tubular cells, impairing salt reabsorption
options.D: Constitutive activation of epithelial sodium channels in principal cells of the collecting duct
options.E: Loss of apical pendrin-mediated chloride-bicarbonate exchange in beta-intercalated cells

new.tested_construct: KCNJ10/Kir4.1 loss reduces basolateral potassium conductance in distal convoluted tubular cells and impairs renal salt reabsorption
new.educational_objective: Recognize EAST/SeSAME syndrome as KCNJ10/Kir4.1 loss of function and connect the renal phenotype to impaired basolateral potassium conductance in distal convoluted tubular cells.

existing.vignette: A 9-year-old boy has epilepsy, gait ataxia, and bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Laboratory studies show persistent hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis despite normal blood pressure. Genetic testing identifies a biallelic loss-of-function variant in KCNJ10.
existing.lead_in: Which of the following renal cellular abnormalities most directly results from this mutation?

options.A: Reduced basolateral potassium conductance in distal convoluted tubule cells
options.B: Loss of the apical sodium-potassium-2 chloride cotransporter in the thick ascending limb
options.C: Loss of apical potassium secretion through ROMK in the thick ascending limb
options.D: Constitutive activation of the epithelial sodium channel in collecting-duct principal cells
options.E: Loss of the apical sodium-chloride cotransporter itself in distal convoluted tubule cells

existing.tested_construct: KCNJ10 encodes the inward-rectifier potassium channel Kir4.1. In the distal convoluted tubule, basolateral Kir4.1-dependent potassium conductance is required for normal epithelial electrical and potassium-sensing physiology that supports sodium-chloride reabsorption. Loss of Kir4.1 produces a salt-wasting tubulopathy with hypokalemia and accompanies the neurologic and auditory phenotype of EAST/SeSAME syndrome.
existing.educational_objective: Link KCNJ10 loss in EAST/SeSAME syndrome to impaired basolateral Kir4.1 potassium conductance in the distal convoluted tubule.

new.vignette: A 24-year-old woman has lifelong compensated hemolysis, splenomegaly, and dehydrated erythrocytes with increased mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration. Her father has similar findings. Sequencing identifies a gain-of-function variant in PIEZO1 that prolongs activity of the mechanically activated cation channel.
new.lead_in: Which downstream ionic sequence most directly causes erythrocyte dehydration in this disorder?

options.A: Reduced calcium entry followed by inhibition of potassium efflux through the Gardos channel
options.B: Increased sodium entry followed by osmotic water influx through aquaporin-1
options.C: Increased chloride entry followed by activation of the erythrocyte sodium-potassium ATPase
options.D: Increased calcium entry followed by activation of the KCa3.1 Gardos channel and loss of potassium and water
options.E: Reduced proton extrusion followed by intracellular alkalinization and water loss

new.tested_construct: PIEZO1-mediated calcium entry activates the KCa3.1 Gardos channel, promoting potassium loss and erythrocyte dehydration
new.educational_objective: Connect PIEZO1 gain of function in hereditary xerocytosis to calcium influx, secondary KCa3.1/Gardos-channel activation, potassium efflux, and osmotic water loss.

existing.vignette: A 22-year-old woman has lifelong compensated hemolysis, mild jaundice, reticulocytosis, and iron overload despite never receiving transfusions. Her mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration is increased, and her erythrocytes have decreased osmotic fragility. Her father has similar findings. Genetic testing identifies a heterozygous pathogenic variant in PIEZO1.
existing.lead_in: Which of the following changes in the mutant protein most directly explains this disorder?

options.A: Loss of spectrin self-association, causing membrane surface-area loss and spherocyte formation
options.B: Failure of the erythrocyte chloride-bicarbonate exchanger, preventing carbon dioxide transport
options.C: Slower inactivation of a mechanically activated cation channel, increasing erythrocyte cation permeability
options.D: Gain-of-function of the erythrocyte Gardos potassium channel, increasing potassium efflux
options.E: Failure of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase to generate reduced glutathione

existing.tested_construct: Gain-of-function PIEZO1 variants slow inactivation or facilitate opening of the mechanically activated cation channel, increasing erythrocyte cation permeability and disrupting red-cell ion/volume homeostasis, which produces cellular dehydration and chronic hemolysis.
existing.educational_objective: Relate PIEZO1 gain-of-function and slowed mechanosensitive-channel inactivation to increased erythrocyte cation permeability and hereditary xerocytosis.

new.vignette: A 2-year-old boy is evaluated after recurrent fasting hypoglycemia and seizures. He has diffuse hyperpigmentation. Morning cortisol is very low and plasma ACTH is markedly elevated, but serum sodium, potassium, plasma renin activity, and aldosterone are normal. Sequencing shows no pathogenic variant in the coding region of MC2R. In cultured adrenal cells, the ACTH receptor is synthesized but fails to reach the plasma membrane.
new.lead_in: Which protein defect most directly explains these findings?

options.A: Loss of steroidogenic acute regulatory protein, preventing mitochondrial cholesterol transport
options.B: Loss of 21-hydroxylase, impairing cortisol and aldosterone synthesis
options.C: Activating mutation of the calcium-sensing receptor, suppressing parathyroid hormone release
options.D: Loss of the glucocorticoid receptor, causing peripheral cortisol resistance
options.E: Loss of MRAP, preventing normal trafficking of the melanocortin-2 ACTH receptor to the cell surface

new.tested_construct: MRAP deficiency preventing trafficking of MC2R/ACTH receptor to the adrenal-cell surface
new.educational_objective: Recognize MRAP as the accessory protein required for MC2R/ACTH-receptor surface trafficking and link its loss to familial glucocorticoid deficiency with preserved mineralocorticoid function.

existing.vignette: A 9-month-old infant has recurrent fasting hypoglycemia and diffuse hyperpigmentation. Serum cortisol is very low and ACTH is markedly elevated. Sodium, potassium, plasma renin activity, and aldosterone are normal. Sequencing of MC2R shows no pathogenic variant, but the infant is homozygous for a loss-of-function variant in MRAP.
existing.lead_in: Which molecular effect most directly causes this patient's cortisol deficiency?

options.A: Failure of the ACTH receptor MC2R to traffic efficiently from the endoplasmic reticulum to the cell surface
options.B: Failure to transport cholesterol from the outer to the inner mitochondrial membrane
options.C: Loss of 21-hydroxylase activity in the adrenal cortex
options.D: Loss of aldosterone synthase activity in the zona glomerulosa
options.E: Constitutive activation of the glucocorticoid receptor in hypothalamic neurons

existing.tested_construct: MRAP is an accessory protein required for normal trafficking and function of the ACTH receptor MC2R; loss causes familial glucocorticoid deficiency type 2 with ACTH resistance and usually preserved mineralocorticoids.
existing.educational_objective: Know that MRAP is required for MC2R trafficking/function and that MRAP loss causes familial glucocorticoid deficiency with isolated ACTH resistance.
